pr_body:
Replaces the previous way of using sorted arrays. Use a simpler way to confirm the visibility of the viewport.

Fix #53776.
Fix #61034.

Supersedes #62938.
Supersedes #63091.

<!--
Please target the `master` branch in priority.
PRs can target `3.x` if the same change was done in `master`, or is not relevant there.

Relevant fixes are cherry-picked for stable branches as needed by maintainers.
You can mention in the description if the change is compatible with `3.x`.
-->
**Edit:**
This patch mainly moves the viewport visibility confirmation logic into a separate function and caches the calculation results. The main part of the logic has not changed, recursion support has been added to support confirmation of parent visibility in the case of `update_mode == RS::VIEWPORT_UPDATE_WHEN_PARENT_VISIBLE`.
pr_comments: A lot of problems are exposed and I'm a bit confused whether they are newly introduced or existing problems.

> A lot of problems are exposed and I'm a bit confused whether they are newly introduced or existing problems.

What do you mean by that? What kind of problems are you running into?

> What do you mean by that? What kind of problems are you running into?

When switching the visibility of the window in the editor, it does not refresh in time, especially when there are multi-level embeddings. Updating an embedded window may not update its embedder. When I add `print_line` to print, it refreshes in time.

By the way, in `RendererViewport`, when a viewport has a non-null parent, does that mean it's embedded?

> When switching the visibility of the window in the editor, it does not refresh in time, especially when there are multi-level embeddings. Updating an embedded window may not update its embedder. When I add `print_line` to print, it refreshes in time.

Does this happen with all update modes? Including UPDATE_MODE_ALWAYS?

> By the way, in `RendererViewport`, when a viewport has a non-null parent, does that mean it's embedded?

I don't think so. I think it just means it is in the scene tree but is non-root

Looking at this change, indeed I think it would only change behavior for `update_mode == RS::VIEWPORT_UPDATE_WHEN_PARENT_VISIBLE`, but in that respect this change makes sense because there is no guarantee in the old approach that the parent viewports visibility was checked and therefor a child viewport may not be updated until the next frame. To be exact, I think this is likely because we would attempt to render the child viewport before we render the parent viewport and thus the order of viewports would check the visibility of the child viewport before the parent viewport.

So i'm not against this change, making the visibility check a recursive function makes sense and may indeed help fix some issues, especially if the parent viewport is set to `RS::VIEWPORT_UPDATE_ONCE`.

Note that this is exactly the scenario reported in #61034 so I would say this would indeed resolve that bug.

> > When switching the visibility of the window in the editor, it does not refresh in time, especially when there are multi-level embeddings. Updating an embedded window may not update its embedder. When I add `print_line` to print, it refreshes in time.
> 
> Does this happen with all update modes? Including UPDATE_MODE_ALWAYS?

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/eac22e3eb489b4a50bb274f10e8a8d4eb795fa99/scene/main/window.cpp#L424-L427

I haven't tested other modes, only the default one, but the above code seems to set the embedded window's update mode to `RS::VIEWPORT_UPDATE_WHEN_PARENT_VISIBLE`
 
> > By the way, in `RendererViewport`, when a viewport has a non-null parent, does that mean it's embedded?
> 
> I don't think so. I think it just means it is in the scene tree but is non-root

I may not have stated clearly, I mean if it has a parent **viewport**. 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/eac22e3eb489b4a50bb274f10e8a8d4eb795fa99/scene/main/window.cpp#L755-L770

This code will make the parent viewport and the embeder inconsistent.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/eac22e3eb489b4a50bb274f10e8a8d4eb795fa99/servers/rendering/renderer_viewport.h#L47-L49

After enabling `gui_embed_subwindow` in parent window, you need to switch the visibility of the subwindow to allow the subwindow to be embedded. So in the above code, `self` and `parent` may be embedded relationships.
@Rindbee Just to add info on the issue linked just above, it seems to be the same/similar issue: the viewport visibility is not detected, but it's not fixed by this PR.

Superseded by #63091.

This only solves the problem of visibility dependencies, not rendering results dependencies. #63091 addresses both issues at the same time.
@Rindbee thank you for your continued work on these issues! While this PR is superceded your work was still very helpful in identifying and resolving the underlying issue.
My pleasure, all for a better Godot.

issue_context.title: Vulkan: SubWindows exhibit rendering artifacts while in the editor (black window)
issue_context.body:
### Godot version

4.0 Alpha 8

### System information

Windows 11 64 Biy Intel Iris Xe Graphics, display/graphics driver version 30.0.100.9864, Vulkan rendering engine

### Issue description

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/105533700/168441490-57e0a45c-1aa5-4b5b-ba91-86857368f3ad.png)
![Screenshot 2022-05-13 220752](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/105533700/168441493-8b52a10e-17e1-41f0-9d18-0398125bc9b1.png)

The window panel nodes are being really weird. Both images were on different days so relaunching does nothing. I don't exactly know how to explain this so here are pics.

### Steps to reproduce

Add a window panel node
Increase size (x:600, y:400 recommended)

### Minimal reproduction project

[Run! 3.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/8693586/Run.3.zip)
comments:
This is a duplicate of another issue, but I can't find it right now.

Can you reproduce this after enabling **Single Window Mode** in the Editor Settings then restarting the editor?

**Single Window Mode** wasn't even on when I made the post.

Also when I relaunched Godot 4 the next day the window was just black, changed back to glitched when I changed the size though.

Edit: Playing the project normally or in debug mode doesn't look glitched; the panel looks fine. Seems to be an editor issue.

I'm confirm having that issue too. See https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/62376
v4.0.alpha10.official [4bbe7f0b9]
Windows 10, GLES3

In the editor, the Window is embedded. So the problem seems to be caused by the following code.

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b3972ad48393559f772151646304e28f938a6fa/scene/main/window.cpp#L424-L427

The update mode will be set to `RS::VIEWPORT_UPDATE_WHEN_PARENT_VISIBLE`. 

https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/9b3972ad48393559f772151646304e28f938a6fa/servers/rendering/renderer_viewport.cpp#L602-L607

The window's `visible` is determined by the above code. When embedded, the child is drawn before the parent. The equality condition does not hold. So, the `visible` will never be `true`.
I believe this has been fixed by #63091

review_comments: Hmm, while extremely unlikely, if an XR viewport is the parent viewport for a viewport set to `RS::VIEWPORT_UPDATE_WHEN_PARENT_VISIBLE`, this would cause `pre_draw_viewport` to be called prematurely and multiple times per frame. That could have unwanted consequences.

It doesn't check multiple times per pass unless `p_pass == 0`. 
```
if (p_viewport->last_pass == p_pass && p_pass) {
	return p_viewport->visible; // Returns the computed cached value.
}
```
The above code can avoid this problem, it will directly use the cached result.
